lightbox: true

All the examples on this page show **real results** for the average day of May in
Cuernavaca, Mexico (the EPW and `materials.ini` used here live in `docs/data/` in the
repository), and are executed when this documentation is rendered. This page covers
the workflow, the materials file, the **1D** examples and the global configuration;
the 2D constructive systems (hollow block, joist-and-block) have their own page:
[Usage — 2D](usage-2d.qmd).

## Workflow

To simulate a wall (or roof) you need to:

1. **Geolocate it** — pass an EPW file to `Location`.
2. **Orient it** — set `azimuth` (and `tilt` if needed: `90` = wall, `0` = roof;
   1D accepts any tilt, with $RF$ varying linearly between both; 2D only 0/90).
3. **Define its solar absorptance** — set `absortance` (intuitively the surface
   color, but coatings of the same visible color can differ in absorptance).
4. **Define its layers** — set `layers` from outside to inside.
5. **Choose the period** — call `location.meanDay(month, year)`.
6. **Compute `Tsa()`**, then choose one solver:
   - **`solve()`** — free-running: the indoor temperature `Ti` evolves with the
     dynamics of the constructive system.
   - **`solveAC()`** — air-conditioned: `Ti` is held at the comfort setpoint and the
     cooling/heating energies are reported.

Both solvers return a `pandas.Series` named `"Ti"`, indexed by time of day on the same
time grid as `Tsa()` — so results concatenate directly
(`pd.concat([data, wall.Tsa()], axis=1)` promotes the named Series to a column. When a `DataFrame` is required, convert with
`wall.solve().to_frame("Ti")`.

> `Tsa` depends on `absortance`, `tilt`, `azimuth`, the month (`meanDay`) and the
> `Location` — the layer stack does **not** affect it. The setters invalidate the
> cache and the next call to `Tsa()` or to a solver recomputes automatically; a
> prior manual `Tsa()` call is optional (useful to inspect the forcing before
> solving).


## Recommended folder structure

A plain text file named `materials.ini` is **required** — EnerHabitat ships with no default materials.

```
project/
├── main.py
├── materials.ini      # Material properties (REQUIRED — user-provided)
└── epw/
    ├── ...
    └── example.epw
```

## Materials file

Material properties are declared in an `.ini` file: the material name is the section
header and `k`, `rho`, `c` the keys (case-sensitive, no Greek letters). Inline comments
(`#` or `;`) are allowed. By default the package looks for `materials.ini` in the
working directory; otherwise set `eh.config.file`.

The file below defines **every material used in these docs** (this page and
[Usage — 2D](usage-2d.qmd)), so you can run all the snippets as-is (values are
typical/illustrative — replace with your own data):

```ini
[Adobe]
k   = 0.58    # Thermal conductivity, W/(m·K)
rho = 1500    # Density, kg/m³
c   = 1480    # Specific heat, J/(kg·K)

[Mortero]     ; cement mortar / render
k   = 0.70
rho = 1800
c   = 1000

[Ladrillo]    ; fired-clay brick
k   = 0.85
rho = 1600
c   = 840

[Concreto]    ; structural concrete (topping, hollow block)
k   = 1.80
rho = 2200
c   = 880

[ConcretoAltaDensidad]   ; high-density structural concrete (joist/rib)
k   = 2.00
rho = 2400
c   = 920

[Bovedilla]   ; lightweight filler block
k   = 0.50
rho = 1200
c   = 900

[Yeso]        ; gypsum plaster
k   = 0.37
rho = 900
c   = 1000

[EPS]         ; expanded polystyrene
k   = 0.04
rho = 15
c   = 1400

[Impermeabilizante]   ; asphaltic waterproofing membrane
k   = 0.17
rho = 1100
c   = 1000
```

Assigning a missing path to `config.file` raises `FileNotFoundError` immediately, and
the previously loaded materials (and path) are kept untouched. If the default
`materials.ini` is not present in the working directory when EnerHabitat is imported,
`materials` starts empty (`{}`) — solving then fails because the layer materials
cannot be resolved — so set `config.file` before building systems.

## Examples

Both modes — free-running and air-conditioned — for the same 1D wall. Setup shared
by all the examples:

<!-- Shared setup for the Usage pages (included by usage.qmd and usage-2d.qmd). -->

::: {#688f0ee2 .cell execution_count=1}
``` {.python .cell-code code-fold="false"}
import enerhabitat as eh
import pandas as pd

eh.config.file = "data/materials.ini"
epw_file = "data/MEX_MOR_Cuernavaca-Matamoros.Intl.AP.767260_TMYx.2004-2018.epw"
```
:::


::: {#7fb28723 .cell execution_count=2}
``` {.python .cell-code code-fold="true" code-summary="Plot helper used by the examples (click to show)"}
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import matplotlib.dates as mdates

EH_COLORS = {"Ti": "#2a78d6", "Tsa": "#eb6834", "Ta": "#008300", "Tn": "#6b7280"}

def plot_day(df, title=""):
    """Temperatures of the average day, with the comfort zone Tn ± DeltaTn."""
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7.2, 3.6))

    # comfort zone: Tn and DeltaTn are columns (constant along the day)
    ax.fill_between(df.index, df["Tn"] - df["DeltaTn"], df["Tn"] + df["DeltaTn"],
                    color=EH_COLORS["Tn"], alpha=0.12, lw=0)
    ax.plot(df["Tn"], color=EH_COLORS["Tn"], ls="--", lw=1, label="Tn ± ΔTn")

    ax.plot(df["Ta"],  color=EH_COLORS["Ta"],  lw=2, label="Ta")
    ax.plot(df["Tsa"], color=EH_COLORS["Tsa"], lw=2, label="Tsa")
    ax.plot(df["Ti"],  color=EH_COLORS["Ti"],  lw=2, label="Ti")

    # tz=... keeps the labels in local time (matplotlib defaults to UTC)
    ax.xaxis.set_major_locator(mdates.HourLocator(byhour=[0, 6, 12, 18], tz=df.index.tz))
    ax.xaxis.set_major_formatter(mdates.DateFormatter("%H", tz=df.index.tz))
    ax.set_xlabel("hour of the average day")
    ax.set_ylabel("temperature (°C)")
    ax.set_title(title, fontsize=10)
    ax.legend(frameon=False, fontsize=9, loc="upper left")
    ax.grid(alpha=0.25, lw=0.5)
    ax.spines["top"].set_visible(False)
    ax.spines["right"].set_visible(False)
    fig.tight_layout()
    plt.show()
```
:::


### 1D wall, free-running

::: {#03cf9dcf .cell execution_count=3}
``` {.python .cell-code}
wall = eh.System(eh.Location(epw_file))
wall.azimuth = 90                    # east-facing
wall.absortance = 0.3
wall.layers = [("Mortero", 0.025), ("Ladrillo", 0.10)]
wall.location.meanDay(month=5, year=2025)
wall.Tsa()

data = wall.solve()                  # free-running Ti
data = pd.concat([data, wall.Tsa()], axis=1)

print(f"energy_transfer = {wall.energy_transfer:,.0f} J/(m²·day)"
      f"  = {wall.energy_transfer/3600:,.0f} Wh/(m²·day)")
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}
```
energy_transfer = 31,973 J/(m²·day)  = 9 Wh/(m²·day)
```
:::
:::


::: {#04f3562a .cell execution_count=4}
``` {.python .cell-code}
plot_day(data, title="Mortero + Ladrillo wall, east, free-running — May, Cuernavaca")
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display}
![](usage_files/figure-html/cell-5-output-1.png){width=681 height=336}
:::
:::


The indoor temperature `Ti` oscillates with a smaller amplitude than the sun–air
temperature `Tsa` and lags behind it — the damping and the delay are the thermal
mass at work.

### 1D wall, air-conditioned

Same wall; `solveAC()` holds `Ti` at the neutrality temperature `Tn` and reports the
energy needed to do so:

::: {#e44071e9 .cell execution_count=5}
``` {.python .cell-code}
dataAC = wall.solveAC()
dataAC = pd.concat([dataAC, wall.Tsa()], axis=1)

print(f"cooling_energy = {wall.cooling_energy:,.0f} J/(m²·day)"
      f"  = {wall.cooling_energy/3600:,.0f} Wh/(m²·day)")
print(f"heating_energy = {wall.heating_energy:,.0f} J/(m²·day)"
      f"  = {wall.heating_energy/3600:,.0f} Wh/(m²·day)")
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}
```
cooling_energy = 943,968 J/(m²·day)  = 262 Wh/(m²·day)
heating_energy = 386,936 J/(m²·day)  = 107 Wh/(m²·day)
```
:::
:::


::: {#c21eed84 .cell execution_count=6}
``` {.python .cell-code}
plot_day(dataAC, title="Same wall, air-conditioned (Ti = Tn) — May, Cuernavaca")
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display}
![](usage_files/figure-html/cell-7-output-1.png){width=681 height=336}
:::
:::


## Configuration

`config` is a global singleton shared by every `Location` and `System`. Changing it
affects **all** subsequent computations.

| Attribute | Default          | Description |
| --------- | ---------------- | ----------- |
| `file`    | `"materials.ini"`| Path to the `.ini` file with material properties |
| `La`      | `2.5` m          | Depth of the indoor air volume |
| `Nx`      | `200`            | Control volumes across the system thickness |
| `ho`      | `13` W/(m²·K)    | Outdoor film coefficient |
| `hi`      | `8.1` W/(m²·K)   | Indoor film coefficient |
| `dt`      | `10` s *(fixed)* | Time step — **not configurable** (assignments are ignored) |

The `ho`/`hi` defaults are the values prescribed by the Mexican standards
**NOM-008-ENER** and **NOM-020-ENER** (`hi = 8.1` is the vertical-surface value,
applied to all orientations); they can be overridden at any time. `dt` is
locked because of the explicit indoor-air coupling — see
[the numerical method](numerics.qmd#indoor-air-coupling-free-running-mode).

```python
eh.config.file = "./materials.ini"
eh.config.La = 2.0
eh.config.ho = 12          # override the NOM defaults if needed
eh.config.reset()          # restore the numeric defaults (La, Nx, ho, hi, dt, air);
                           # config.file / materials are user-provided and are kept
```

`config.materials` is a read-only dict keyed by material name
(`eh.config.materials["Adobe"].k`, `.rho`, `.c`).

The 2D-only parameters (mesh and convergence) live in `config2d` — see
[Usage — 2D](usage-2d.qmd#config2d-2d-mesh-and-convergence).
